world.b: The International Campaign to Ban Landmines recorded 6,929 casualties in 2025, 84% of them civilians and half of those children, driven largely by Myanmar's civil war.
world.title: Global landmine casualties hit a five-year high, driven by Myanmar, Syria

world.h: UN: 47,000 women killed by partners or family
world.b: About 47,000 women and girls were killed by an intimate partner or family member last year, the UN's 2026 Femicide Brief found, and home remains the most dangerous place for them.
world.title: Five women killed every hour globally by partner, relative last year: UN

world.h: LIVE: Three ships catch fire after hitting Hormuz mines
world.b: Iran says three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Follow Al Jazeera's live coverage of the US-Israel war on Iran.
world.title: Houthi attack on Riyadh tower leaves 11 injured, Saudi authorities say

world.h: Iran vows to use 'all available means' against US blockade
world.b: Iran says it will use all means at its disposal to counter the US naval blockade imposed during the nine-month US-Israel war on Iran.

national.h: Princeton researcher held by ICE at D.C. airport
national.b: ICE detained Chinese doctoral student Eva Yi Xie at Reagan National Airport; DHS says she overstayed her visa.
national.title: Chinese neuroscientist at Princeton held by ICE after detention at D.C. airport

national.h: Army to detonate lead azide in Iowa Wednesday
national.b: After winning approval from a federal appeals court, the Army plans a controlled detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning.

national.h: ProPublica: Ambetter prior authorization hurt patients
national.b: A ProPublica investigation found the popular insurance plan's use of prior authorization led to delayed cancer treatment and missed medication.
national.title: Delayed Cancer Treatment. Missed Medication. How a Popular Insurance Plan’s Use of Prior Authorization Hurt Patients.

national.h: Doctors struggle as parents refuse vitamin K
national.b: At a Grand Rapids hospital, at least one family a day on average refuses the vitamin K injection for their newborn.
national.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K

national.h: Medical debt could get worse, experts warn
national.b: Millions of Americans carry medical debt, and experts worry high inflation, health costs and lost insurance will push the number higher.
national.title: Millions of Americans have medical debt. Experts worry the problem is about to get worse

national.b: The state health department confirmed the death of an unvaccinated Centre County resident who tested positive for measles, bringing the outbreak's death toll to nine.

national.h: Military families share challenges as commission meets
national.b: As Trump's new military spouse commission convenes, families describe problems like expired groceries at overseas base commissaries.
national.title: What military families see as their biggest challenges as Trump’s new military spouse commission convenes

national.h: Trump calls to speed up federal executions
national.b: At the Justice Department, Trump reaffirmed his support for the death penalty and attacked California Gov. Gavin Newsom.

national.h: Tech outages lead some New Yorkers to stock up
national.b: After a series of technology outages this month, some New York City residents are keeping cash, water and supplies on hand in case disruptions last longer.

national.h: Leaked plan targets American History museum
national.b: A D.C. Metro rider photographed a draft 'Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan' calling for executive firings and sweeping changes at the National Museum of American History.
national.title: Spotted on the D.C. Metro: Trump Staffer Accidentally Reveals Plan for Smithsonian Overhaul

national.h: Glitches and storms threaten Thanksgiving travel
national.b: Recent airline outages, storms on both coasts and soaring airfares could make holiday travel chaotic, and an East Coast storm could ground balloons at the 100th Macy's parade.

national.h: States race to explain new Medicaid work requirements
national.b: Starting next year, roughly 20 million people will need to prove they're working, volunteering, in school or exempt to keep Medicaid under last year's tax and spending law.

national.h: Immigrant abuse survivors weigh calling 911 against deportation
national.b: Amid an immigration crackdown in west Michigan, ProPublica heard from immigrant women in abusive relationships about how they calculate their safety. Some are afraid to leave the house.
national.title: If They Call 911 About Domestic Abuse, Will They Be Deported?

politics.h: Abortion-rights Democrats won, but big changes unlikely
politics.b: Democrats lack full control in states with the strictest bans, and any congressional move would likely face a Trump veto.
politics.title: Democrats supporting abortion rights won big in midterms, but vast changes unlikely soon

politics.b: Democrats eyeing the White House see Trump's pressure on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as fresh evidence of his coziness with tech executives.

politics.h: Unsealed records detail search of Ilhan Omar's home
politics.b: Court documents show the magistrate judge who approved the search ruled Omar could assert privacy protections for sitting members of Congress.

politics.h: Democrats widen probe of Trump Jr.-linked firm
politics.b: Led by Rep. Jamie Raskin, Democrats are expanding their investigation into 1789 Capital, which investigators say grew from $150 million to $3 billion in managed assets after Trump Jr. joined.
politics.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access

politics.b: As counting wraps up in the final midterm races, Democrats hold 258 of 435 House seats with four races uncalled, and the party plans to use its majorities for oversight.

politics.h: Congress erupts over Huang's return to Nvidia
politics.b: Lawmakers from both parties criticized Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Trump's urging; Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

politics.h: Appeals court opens path to erase Trump conviction
politics.b: A 2nd Circuit panel moved Trump's hush money case toward federal court, where he could seek dismissal on presidential immunity grounds.

politics.h: Leadership fight tests new Democratic senators
politics.b: The 13 incoming Democratic senators must choose between keeping Chuck Schumer as leader or backing challenger Chris Van Hollen, testing their campaign promises of change.

politics.h: Universal healthcare rises on Democrats' agenda
politics.b: Democrats plan swift action in the new Congress to reverse recent Medicaid cuts and revive Affordable Care Act tax breaks, with more ambitious universal healthcare goals behind them.
The Democratic National Committee announced Monday a dozen presidential primary debates for an expected crowded 2028 field, with the first scheduled for June.

politics.h: Oath Keepers founder Stewart Rhodes says he's 'done' with Trump
politics.b: Stewart Rhodes, who went to prison for his role in Jan. 6, now calls Trump a traitor and "one of the very worst in our nation's history."

politics.h: California voters reject billionaire tax despite progressive wins
politics.b: 52% of voters rejected Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' wealth, and they narrowly approved a measure making such taxes much harder to enact in the future.

international.h: Cameroon separatist pleads not guilty in Norway
international.b: Lucas Cho Ayaba denied charges in an Oslo court of being an accessory to war crimes and terrorism over two attacks in Cameroon.
international.title: Cameroon separatist leader pleads not guilty at war crimes trial in Norway

international.h: Putin vows retaliation over refinery strikes
international.b: Putin said Ukraine kept attacking Russian oil refineries despite Trump's requests to hold off, and threatened retaliation.
international.title: Putin says retaliation ‘inevitable’ after Ukraine hit Russian oil plants

international.h: Turkish military helicopter crash kills five
international.b: An air force AS-532 helicopter crashed after taking off from Eskisehir on a training flight, killing five crew members, the defense ministry said.
international.title: Turkish military helicopter crash kills five in western Turkiye

international.h: Pope Francis' diary reveals spiritual crisis
international.b: Diary excerpts published by the Vatican describe Francis seeing the 'gates of hell' over the abuse scandal and a spiritual crisis in 2021-22.

international.h: UK heat deaths hit record high
international.b: The UK Health Security Agency estimates more than 5,000 deaths were linked to this summer's heat, the most since its reports began in 2016.

international.h: Iraq moves to take over Kurdish-held oilfields
international.b: Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the oil ministry to manage oilfields in Kurdish-controlled areas of Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahuddin and Nineveh provinces.

international.h: Projectile hits Riyadh tower, injuring 11
international.b: Saudi Civil Defence said an unspecified projectile struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district, injuring 11 people.

international.h: Two arrested after break-in at Prince William's home
international.b: Police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespass after a break-in at Anmer Hall on the Sandringham estate; the house was unoccupied.

international.h: China probes Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
international.b: The Politburo member is the fourth from the top leadership body investigated since last year, suspected of 'severe violations of discipline and laws,' Xinhua said.
international.title: China probes Shanghai party chief Chen Jining over corruption

international.h: Malaysia to send 6,500 Rohingya back to Myanmar
international.b: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the repatriations five days after the World Court ruled Myanmar's forces committed genocide against the Rohingya.

international.h: Hasina plans Dec. 16 return to Bangladesh
international.b: Ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia, plans to return from exile in India; the government says she can only return through extradition.

international.h: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill at least 7
international.b: At least seven Palestinians, including a child and police officers, were killed in Israeli air strikes on Gaza as doctors warn of a meningitis outbreak.

international.h: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills two
international.b: A dawn air attack killed two people and wounded more than 40, including an infant, a day after Kyiv said its drones sank a Russian warship in a Libyan port.

international.h: Australia threatens tech giants with big fines
international.b: Communications Minister Anika Wells announced plans for heavier fines on tech companies that fail to remove harmful content from their platforms.

international.h: WHO chief visits Cuba's ailing hospitals
international.b: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus toured a pediatric cardiology center in Havana as Cuba's healthcare system deteriorates amid an economic crisis deepened by US sanctions.

international.h: Guterres urges global AI oversight within a year
international.b: Speaking at a conference in Barbados, the UN secretary-general called on member states to build a multilateral AI risk framework backed by independent oversight within the next year.

international.h: Bukele names soldiers killed in Haiti
international.b: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele identified the three Salvadoran soldiers killed on an anti-gang mission in Haiti.

international.h: Mexico to try 'El Chapo Isidro' at home
international.b: Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores will be tried in Mexico despite a US extradition request.

international.h: 12,000 evacuated from Manchester concert
international.b: More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a Don Toliver concert at Manchester's Co-op Live arena and over 80 were treated after an unknown irritant was released in the crowd, police said.

international.h: At least 15 killed in Kyiv region as Russia steps up attacks
international.b: The death toll from Russian attacks in Ukraine's Kyiv region has risen to at least 15, including at a partially destroyed apartment building in the town of Dymer.

international.h: Rights group says attacks on West Bank medics up 350%
international.b: Physicians for Human Rights Israel says Palestinian healthcare staff in the occupied West Bank are increasingly coming under attack from Israeli soldiers and settlers.

international.h: Belgian strike set to ground nearly all flights
international.b: Belgium's air traffic controller Skeyes said its staff will join a national strike against austerity measures, suspending regular service at the country's airports from 7am to 9pm Monday.

international.h: Indonesia confirms 24 dead in candy factory fire
international.b: Authorities confirmed 24 deaths in the fire that gutted the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province, with about 30 people still missing. A presidential adviser said a short circuit in an air conditioner may be to blame.

international.h: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian ship off Libya
international.b: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Ukraine sank the Russian ship Merkury off the Libyan coast, hailing an "exemplary Ukrainian operation" after the strike at Benghazi port.

business.h: Afghan refugees build businesses in Houston
business.b: Thousands of Afghans who resettled in the Houston area after the 2021 US withdrawal have built a growing network of businesses.
business.title: From refugees to entrepreneurs: Afghan businesses take root in Houston

business.h: Nvidia recovers most of its lost value
business.b: Nvidia had regained $952 billion of the $1.16 trillion in market value it lost when Jensen Huang resigned, according to a Financial Times analysis.
business.title: Nvidia stock cools after Huang’s return-driven surge

business.h: Few US homes are protected against floods
business.b: Very few homeowners outside flood zones buy flood insurance, even as storms bring flooding to the Bay Area, the East Coast and Florida.
business.title: As climate change causes more flooding, most American homes aren't protected

business.h: Inside Trump's latest meme coin dinner
business.b: Two crypto investors who attended the president's meme coin dinner on Sunday gave NPR inside access; the dinners have sparked intense controversy.
business.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well

business.h: Record share of firms report rising material costs
business.b: 82% of businesses said their material costs went up, the highest share since the National Association for Business Economics survey began in 1999.

business.h: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler for nearly $44 billion
business.b: The all-stock deal is part of a wave of cybersecurity mergers as companies grow to better protect against AI-driven threats.

business.h: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman
business.b: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman, saying it is in the best interest of the company.

business.h: What Thanksgiving dinner costs this year
business.b: Grocery prices have risen nearly 22% over five years, driven by wars, tariffs and severe weather, but food-price experts say it's unclear whether this year's Thanksgiving meal will cost more.

business.h: Seniors embrace Tesla's automated driving despite safety concerns
business.b: Older drivers are using Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to stay on the road longer, but safety experts warn the company may be overselling what its cars can do.
business.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety

business.h: Meta's AI chief warns superintelligence is 'arriving'
business.b: Meta's top AI executive warned that superintelligence far exceeding human intellect is imminent and sounded the alarm about the risk of humanity losing control of AI.

business.h: Asian markets slide as AI bubble fears mount
business.b: Markets in South Korea, Hong Kong and mainland China fell deeper on Monday, extending Friday's tech-led sell-off. Seoul's Kospi slid as much as 5.8 percent before paring losses.

science.h: Eagles may have hunted adult baboons
science.b: Raptor damage on adult male baboon bones from Chad suggests birds of prey can take primates as big as some early human ancestors.
science.title: Eagles can prey on adult baboons. Did our ancestors face that threat?

science.h: After surgery, man sees his cat's eyes on people
science.b: Following 2024 brain surgery, a 29-year-old teacher began seeing features of faces he'd seen before, including his cat's eyes, on other people's faces.
science.title: This man sometimes sees his cat’s eyes on people’s faces

science.b: Psychologist Ryon McDermott spent seven years building a scale to measure masculinity in a positive light, a push that is dividing the male studies field.
science.title: The notion of 'positive masculinity' is dividing the male studies field

science.h: Mushroom supplements promise a lot. What does the science say?
science.b: NPR looks at the evidence behind popular mushroom supplements such as lion's mane and reishi.

science.h: What makes Challenger Deep the ocean's deepest spot
science.b: The roughly 11,000-meter valley in the Mariana Trench sits where the Pacific plate dives beneath the Mariana plate. Researchers are working out why it runs deeper than other subduction zones.
science.title: Motion under the ocean explains the depth of the world’s deepest spot

goodnews.h: Pakistan's first astronaut set to launch
goodnews.b: Air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is poised to become Pakistan's first person in space, joining China's Shenzhou-24 mission to the Tiangong space station.
Independent mathematicians say they have full confidence in Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis, developed with the AI tool Claude.
goodnews.title: Math’s holy grail, the Riemann hypothesis, appears solved with AI’s help

local.b: Forecasters expect rain and winds gusting to 60 mph on Thanksgiving, which could affect the 100th parade's balloons.
local.title: Goodbye Kitty: Preparation underway for a windy Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in NYC

local.h: Body shop owner charged in tow truck scheme
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors say Steven Ventura used unlicensed tow trucks to haul crash victims' cars and demand bogus storage fees.
local.title: Brooklyn body shop owner charged with bilking drivers in illegal tow truck scheme

local.h: Woman stabbed at random in Riverside Park
local.b: Police are searching for a man who stabbed a 26-year-old woman near West 96th Street Monday night; she is in stable condition.
local.title: NYPD searches for suspect who police say stabbed a woman at random in Riverside Park

local.h: Lawsuit says co-signer firm inflates rents
local.b: A class action accuses TheGuarantors of raising renters' costs through exclusive deals with landlords that block cheaper options.
local.title: NYC renters face ‘higher fees, reduced housing access’ due to co-signer company, lawsuit says

local.h: Report backs regular taxi fare hikes
local.b: A Taxi and Limousine Commission report says yellow cab operating costs rose about 16% since 2022, and regular fare hikes could help drivers avoid poverty.
local.title: Fare hikes on yellow taxi cabs could keep drivers out of poverty, city report finds

local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul vetoed a bill requiring AI platforms to warn users their information may be inaccurate, calling it too far-reaching.
local.title: NY Gov. Hochul vetoes bill that would have required AI accuracy warnings

local.b: Nearly three weeks after a Nov. 4 ransomware attack, the Queens Public Library has its website, app, computers and digital collections back up.
local.title: Queens Public Library restores most services nearly 3 weeks after ransomware attack

local.h: Flu cases surge ahead of Thanksgiving
local.b: More than 43,000 New Yorkers have caught the flu since early October, compared with about 7,000 at this point last season, state data shows.
local.title: Reported flu cases surge across New York ahead of Thanksgiving

local.h: NY sues HUD over mixed-status housing rule
local.b: The state and city sued over a federal rule that could strip housing assistance from about 20,000 families in which not every member is a citizen or eligible non-citizen.
local.title: NYC, state sue Trump administration over ‘mixed-status’ federal housing assistance rule

local.h: Top court upholds Section 8 renter protection
local.b: New York's Court of Appeals upheld a state law banning discrimination against tenants who pay rent with housing subsidies, siding with Attorney General Letitia James against an Ithaca landlord.
local.title: New York’s highest court upholds key protection for low-income renters with Section 8

local.h: New film captures ICE agents' banter at NYC courthouse arrests
local.b: Journalist Emma V.F. filmed scores of arrests at 26 Federal Plaza, along with the rarely seen small talk among the ICE agents making them.
local.title: New film captures ICE agents' banter amid NYC courthouse arrests

local.h: Citi Bike e-bike rides to be capped at $3.65 for members
local.b: Under a new deal between Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration and Lyft, Citi Bike members will pay no more than $3.65 for e-bike rides up to 45 minutes starting Jan. 19, 2027.
local.title: NYC Citi Bike member rides to be capped at $3.65 after Mamdani inks new deal with Lyft

periods.name: Tonight
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 39. North wind around 10 mph.

periods.name: Wednesday
periods.text: Increasing clouds, with a high near 50. Northeast wind around 11 mph.

periods.name: Wednesday Night
periods.text: Cloudy, with a steady temperature around 49. Breezy, with a northeast wind 11 to 16 mph increasing to 19 to 24 mph after midnight.

periods.name: Thanksgiving Day
periods.text: Rain, mainly after 1pm.  High near 55. Windy, with a northeast wind 26 to 33 mph, with gusts as high as 55 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between a half and three quarters of an inch possible.

periods.name: Thursday Night
periods.text: Rain.  Low around 53. Windy, with an east wind 26 to 34 mph becoming south after midnight.  Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between three quarters and one inch possible.

periods.name: Friday
periods.text: A 50 percent chance of rain.  Mostly cloudy, with a high near 58. Breezy.

localgood.b: Green-Wood Cemetery fellows are sifting soil to catalogue potentially thousands of unknown fungus species.
localgood.title: Digging up a secret world under a Brooklyn graveyard, one teaspoon at a time

localgood.h: About 100 New Yorkers ditched their smartphones for a month
localgood.b: A phone-free party celebrated roughly 100 New Yorkers who gave up their smartphones for a month, with a showcase of the hobbies and art projects they picked up instead.
localgood.title: These New Yorkers ditched their smartphones for a month. No, seriously.
